category_edits.rationale: Hypothesis: mildly attenuating frequent history items will reduce their dominance and improve macro validation HR@10. Scale only input item embeddings by clip((training_count / median_positive_count)^(-0.1), 0.75, 1.25). Keep learned embeddings, candidate scoring, Transformer topology, readout, loss and optimizer unchanged. Save counts and scales as checkpoint buffers; the embedded predictor already imports this SASRec class and restores both through load_state_dict. Apply identically across all four datasets, retaining one model per category.

# Frequency features use only the supplied training interactions.
    item_counts = np.zeros(itemnum + 1, dtype=np.int64)
    for items in user_train.values():
        np.add.at(item_counts, np.asarray(items, dtype=np.int64), 1)
    item_counts[0] = 0
    observed = item_counts > 0
    positive_counts = item_counts[observed]
    median_count = float(np.median(positive_counts)) if positive_counts.size else 1.0
    # Zero-count nonpadding items take the clipped upper limit.
    history_scale = np.full(itemnum + 1, 1.25, dtype=np.float32)
    history_scale[observed] = np.clip(
        (item_counts[observed].astype(np.float64) / median_count) ** (-0.1),
        0.75, 1.25,
    ).astype(np.float32)
    history_scale[0] = 1.0
    with torch.no_grad():
        model.item_train_counts.copy_(torch.as_tensor(item_counts, device=device))
        model.history_item_scale.copy_(torch.as_tensor(history_scale, device=device))

    optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=LR, weight_decay=WEIGHT_DECAY, betas=(0.9, 0.98))
